props.text: Two of the West's biggest tourism airports, and there's still no direct flight between Las Vegas and Aspen — you'll connect through Denver. Flying out of LAS, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $1,096 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Cancún — nonstop, ~4h30m
features.text: Southwest flies it direct, but only about 5 flights a week — worth booking around the schedule.

features.title: Oaxaca — no nonstop
features.text: Routes via Mexico City or Houston; total travel runs 8h05m–9h26m.

features.title: Aspen — no nonstop
features.text: Despite both being major Mountain West leisure hubs, there's no direct link — expect a connection through Denver adding several hours.

props.text: Cancún's nonstop makes it the obvious beach-reset counter-trip to the Strip. Oaxaca is the bigger commitment of the three — no nonstop exists, which suits travelers wanting an authentic food-and-culture trip as a real contrast to casino tourism. The genuine surprise is Aspen: two of the West's biggest tourism airports, and still no direct air link between them.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Is there a direct flight from Vegas to Aspen?
items.answer: No — despite both being major western leisure hubs, there's no nonstop route; expect a connection, commonly through Denver, adding several hours each way.

items.question: Is Cancún easy from Vegas?
items.answer: There's a nonstop on Southwest, but it only runs about 5 times a week, so it's worth booking around the schedule rather than assuming daily availability.
